title: Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science Module 4 – Human Impacts
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science Module 4. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What term describes water that is safe enough for humans to drink?
What is wastewater from homes and toilets called?
What is rainwater that flows over roads and other surfaces into drains called?
What process removes contaminants from wastewater so it can be safely discharged or reused?
What term means using treated water again instead of discarding it?
What human activity removes water from rivers or groundwater faster than it is naturally replaced?
What term describes an excessive growth of algae in a water body?
What nutrient enrichment process can lead to algal blooms in waterways?
What dissolved gas may fall to harmful levels when large algal blooms decompose?
What term describes water stored below Earth’s surface in pores and cracks?
What term describes the build-up of salts in soil?
What process removes soil by agents such as water or wind?
What land-clearing practice can increase erosion by removing protective plant cover?
questions.answer: Deforestation. Accept: vegetation clearing or land clearing.

questions.prompt: What agricultural practice reduces erosion by following the natural contours of a slope?
What process aims to restore damaged land so it can function more effectively again?
What term describes the presence of harmful substances in soil?
What group of metallic pollutants includes lead, mercury and cadmium?
What agricultural chemicals used to kill pests can contaminate soil if misused?
What term describes removing or neutralising contaminants from polluted soil?
What process uses living organisms, often microbes or plants, to reduce environmental contamination?
What term describes a species moved by humans to an area where it did not naturally occur?
What term describes an introduced species that spreads and causes environmental, economic or social harm?
What introduced Australian predator has contributed to the decline of many native animals?
What ecological interaction occurs when an introduced species and a native species need the same limited resource?
What broad term describes actions used to reduce the population or impact of an introduced species?
questions.answer: Control. Accept: mitigation or species control.

finalRound.prompt: What term means using natural resources in a way that meets present needs without preventing future generations from meeting theirs?
